```{r}
data(aids)
data(aids.id)
```

```{r}
km_fit2 <- survfit(Surv(Time, death) ~ drug, data = aids.id)

km_fit2

ggsurvplot(km_fit2, 
           data = aids.id,
           pval = TRUE,             # Adds the log-rank test p-value to the plot
           risk.table = TRUE,       # Adds a table showing patients left over time
           conf.int = TRUE,
           legend.title = "Treatment",
           legend.labs = c("ddC", "ddl"),
           xlab = "Time in Days",
           title = "Kaplan-Meier Survival Estimate for AIDS")
```

```{r}
cox_aids <- coxph(Surv(Time, death) ~ drug + gender + CD4, data = aids.id)
summary(cox_aids)
```

```{r}

aids %>%
  select(CD4_sqr) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything()) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
```

```{r}
glmm_CD4 <- mixed_model(CD4_sqr ~ obstime + obstime:drug, 
                        random = ~ obstime | patient, 
                        data = aids,
                        family = negative.binomial)
summary(glmm_CD4)
```

```{r}
cox_aids2 <- coxph(Surv(Time, death) ~ drug + gender, data = aids.id)

summary(cox_aids2)
```

```{r}
joint_fit2 <- jm(cox_aids2, glmm_CD4, time_var = "obstime", n_iter = 15000, n_burnin = 2500)

summary(joint_fit2)
```

```{r}
# 1. Randomly select exactly 4 patients to match the 2x2 grid layout
set.seed(129) 
random_patients <- sample(aids.id$patient, 4)

# 2. Set up the graphics window for a 2x2 grid with adjusted margins
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

# 3. Loop through the 4 patients and generate both longitudinal and survival panels
for (pid in random_patients) {
  
  # Extract this specific patient's chart
  pt_data <- aids[aids$patient == pid, ]
  
  # Forecast their CD4 count trajectory
  pred_long <- predict(joint_fit2, newdata = pt_data, return_newdata = TRUE)
  
  # Forecast their survival/event risk
  pred_event <- predict(joint_fit2, newdata = pt_data, process = "event", return_newdata = TRUE)
  
  # Plot the dual-panel output with explicit Patient ID titles
  plot(pred_long, pred_event, 
       main = paste("Patient ID:", pid),
       xlim = c(0, 25))     
}

# 4. Reset the plotting window back to normal when finished
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2))
```

```{r}
# Calculate the Time-Dependent ROC curve
roc_quiz <- tvROC(joint_fit2, newdata = aids, Tstart = 6, Dt = 6, cores = 1)

# Print the Area Under the Curve (AUC) score
summary(roc_quiz)

# Plot the ROC curve
plot(roc_quiz)
```

```{r}
tvAUC(joint_fit2, newdata = aids, Tstart = 6, Dt = 6, cores = 1)

# Calculate the Brier Score to check prediction accuracy
brier_quiz <- tvBrier(joint_fit2, newdata = aids, Tstart = 6, Dt = 6)

# Print the result
brier_quiz
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)
unique_ids <- unique(aids$patient)
n_folds <- 5

# Create a balanced, randomized vector of fold assignments (1 through 5)
folds <- sample(rep(1:n_folds, length.out = length(unique_ids)))

cv_auc <- numeric(n_folds)
cv_brier <- numeric(n_folds)

# 2. Run the actual refitting loop
for (i in 1:n_folds) {
  cat("Running Fold", i, "of", n_folds, "...\n")
  
  # Identify train and test IDs
  test_ids <- unique_ids[folds == i]
  train_ids <- unique_ids[folds != i]
  
  # Split longitudinal and survival datasets strictly by patient ID
  train_data    <- aids[aids$patient %in% train_ids, ]
  train_data.id <- aids.id[aids.id$patient %in% train_ids, ]
  test_data     <- aids[aids$patient %in% test_ids, ]
  
  # Refit the strictly correct Negative Binomial using Gauss-Kronrod quadrature
  nb_fit <- mixed_model(CD4_sqr ~ obstime + obstime:drug, 
                        random = ~ obstime | patient, 
                        data = train_data,
                        family = negative.binomial)
  
  # Refit the survival submodel
  cox_fit <- coxph(Surv(Time, death) ~ drug + gender, data = train_data.id)
  
  # Refit the joint model
  fold_jm <- jm(cox_fit, nb_fit, time_var = "obstime", n_iter = 8000, n_burnin = 1300)
  summary(fold_jm)
  
  # Test on the remaining 20% unseen data (cores = 1 to prevent socket crashes)
  cv_auc[i]   <- tvAUC(fold_jm, newdata = test_data, Tstart = 6, Dt = 6, cores = 1)$auc
  cv_brier[i] <- tvBrier(fold_jm, newdata = test_data, Tstart = 6, Dt = 6, cores = 1)$Brier
}

# 3. See the true, un-cheated cross-validation scores
cat("\n5-Fold CV AUC:", mean(cv_auc, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("5-Fold CV Brier:", mean(cv_brier, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
```
